title: Candidate ranking annotator guidelines and slice specification
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is the working annotator + analysis protocol used to collect pairwise preference labels and produce NDCG-based reranking evaluation sets for model onboarding. It covers sampling strategy, annotation UI guidance, label taxonomy, overlap/QC rules, expected inter-annotator agreement, slice definitions, and the downstream aggregation pipeline (NDGC@k, pairwise-to-score bookkeeping). Use this for: new model onboarding evaluations, regression checks, and slice-level performance tracking.

High-level goals:
- Produce reliable pairwise preference labels between model candidate rankings with reproducible export schema.
- Ensure slices capture common failure modes for rerankers (query length, user intent, entity-heavy, low-surface-signal).
- Maintain annotation quality with sentinel items and overlap to measure agreement and drift.
- Provide clear recipes for NDCG@k calculation and how to convert pairwise labels to graded relevance.

Sampling strategy and dataset composition:
- Sample sources: production traffic (10% sample window), synthetic diagnostic queries, and replayed customer test suites.
- Candidate set: for each request pick N=10 retrieved candidates (diversified) and retain the top 5 as the primary ranking to be evaluated. If fewer than 5 candidates exist, pad with placeholders and mark as "no-result".
- Stratified sampling by: query token length (buckets: 1-3, 4-8, 9-20, >20), user intent (informational, navigational, transactional, conversational), and recency (session-first vs session-followup). Aim final eval set sizes: 4k production queries, 1k synthetic adversarial, 1k curated enterprise/regulatory test cases.
- Overlap: 15% pair overlap between annotators (randomly selected pairs) for agreement measurement. 3% sentinel items inserted per batch for QC.

Annotation UI and instructions (pairwise mode):
- Present annotators with: query + context (if multi-turn: last 3 turns) and two anonymized candidates (A/B). Show candidate text, source id, and any structured metadata (length, snippet highlight).
- Primary question: "Which candidate would you prefer to surface for this query in terms of usefulness to the user?" Choices: A, B, Tie.
- Secondary quick flags (optional): hallucination, unsafe, irrelevant, contains-PII. These are checkbox multi-labels for error diagnosis but NOT used in primary score.
- Time guidance: spend ~30–90s per pair. If you cannot decide after 90s mark Tie and move on.
- Prefer shorter, decisive answers: if A directly answers the query while B is vague, choose A even if B is more fluent. Relevance trumps fluency.
- Tie policy: mark tie when both candidates are equally useful or equally unusable. If one has a clear factual error, mark the other even if it is longer. If both hallucinate the same false claim, mark Tie unless one gives a corrective signal.

Label taxonomy (for exports):
- pair_label: "A" | "B" | "Tie"
- tie_reason (optional): "equal_relevance" | "equal_hallucination" | "insufficient_info"
- error_flags: list of error codes ("HALL", "UNSAFE", "PII", "IRREL")
- annotator_id: string
- pair_id: string (UUID)
- seed_request_id: string (original request id)
- timestamp: ISO8601

Converting pairwise labels to graded relevance (for NDCG):
- We use a simple aggregation to convert pairwise outcomes into a 0-2 graded relevance scale per candidate per query. Process:
  1) For each query, compute Elo-like Bradley-Terry wins for candidates using pairwise outcomes (treat Tie as half-win to both).
  2) Normalize resulting scores to [0,1].
  3) Map normalized score to grades: [0.67,1.0] => grade 2 (highly relevant), [0.33,0.67) => grade 1 (relevant), [0,0.33) => grade 0 (not relevant).
- Rationale: direct binary wins are noisy with many ties; the BT/Elo smoothing gives more stable graded relevance for NDCG.

NDCG calculation details:
- We compute NDCG@1, @3, @5. Discounted Gain uses log2 positional discount: gain = (2^{grade} - 1). DCG_k = sum_{i=1..k} (gain_i / log2(i+1)). IDCG is computed using best-possible ordering under true grades. Normalized NDCG = DCG/IDCG.
- Report both mean NDCG and median NDCG across queries. Provide per-slice NDCG and delta against baseline model version.
- Bootstrapped 95% CI: resample queries 1000x, compute mean NDCG distribution, report percentile CI.

Slice definitions (priority slices to populate in eval exports):
- short-query: token_count <= 3.
- long-query: token_count > 20.
- multi-turn-context: has_context=true and context_turns>=2.
- entity-heavy: candidate contains >=2 named entities and query references named entities.
- low-surface-signal: query's avg token IdF in top-5 retrieved docs < threshold (requires precomputed idf).
- ambiguous-intent: queries with >1 likely intent cluster score (fuzzy intent entropy > 0.6).
- enterprise-regulated: contains keywords from compliance list (PII, SSN, HIPAA terms).
- hallucination-sensitive: any candidate flagged HALL by >10% of annotators in overlap set.
- long-answer-required: expected answer length > 200 chars in golden references.
- sensitive: safety/unsafe content flagged in any annotator comment.
- platform-specific: mobile-optimized vs desktop (derived from request metadata).

Analysis and reporting templates:
- Primary sheet columns for downstream analysts (flat CSV):
  request_id, query, candidate_rank, candidate_text, candidate_id, grade (0/1/2), bt_score, pair_wins, annotator_ids, slice_tags (semicolon-separated), error_flags, model_version, export_batch, timestamp
- Per-batch KPIs: mean NDCG@5, delta vs baseline, % queries with zero high-grade candidates, % hallucination flags, pairwise agreement (Krippendorff alpha), annotator time distribution (median/sec).
- Regression alert rules (auto):
  * Absolute NDCG@5 drop > 0.03 and p-value < 0.01 (bootstrap) triggers high-priority regression.
  * Any slice drop > 0.05 NDCG@k triggers investigation ticket.
  * Hallucination rate increase > 20% relative triggers content-review.

QC and annotator calibration:
- Calibration run for new annotators: 50 gold pairs with known consensus. Require >= 80% match on non-tie items and Cohen's kappa > 0.6 on overlap before contributing to production labeling.
- Ongoing QC: random 15% overlap across annotators per batch, 3% sentinel insertion. Annotator batches failing more than 2 sentinels or kappa < 0.5 in last 200 pairs are paused and reviewed.
- Drift detection: weekly summary of per-annotator bias toward Tie or preferring longer responses. If an annotator has >2 std dev bias, flag for retraining.

Export and file naming conventions:
- File format: UTF-8 CSV with columns described above. Also store raw pairwise JSON for traceability (one JSON per pair).
- Naming: rr-eval_v{model_version}_{export_date}_{slice-tag}.csv
  Example: rr-eval_v2.7_2025-03-20_enterprise-regulated.csv

Examples (short):
- Query: "renew passport steps"
  Candidate A: step-by-step list from gov portal -> choose A (useful, actionable).
  Candidate B: high-level history of passports -> choose A.
- Query: "best places to eat" (ambiguous)
  Candidate A: top-10 curated restaurants with locations -> choose A if query geolocation matches.
  Candidate B: generic food blog -> Tie if both are similar usefulness or choose A if local context present.

Operational notes for analysts and engineers:
- Keep seed_request_id ↔︎ production log mapping for traceability; logging must include model conds, randomness seeds, and retrieval snapshot.
- Provide the BT conversion code as a small service; keep parameters (k-factor, tie weight) configurable and logged per export.
- When comparing models, freeze candidate retrieval at baseline to isolate reranker change effects unless testing full-stack changes.

Open questions / TODO (working list):
- Validate mapping thresholds for grade bins (0.33/0.67) on historical datasets — is a three-grade mapping optimal for NDCG sensitivity?
- Evaluate alternate incentives: gather graded labels directly instead of pairwise to shorten pipeline; measure annotation cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Expand slice set for locale/translation failures (non-en) and for tokenization edge-cases.

Appendix: quick checklist for launching a rerank eval export
- [ ] Confirm sample spec and query size quota
- [ ] Prepare candidate snapshot and anonymize model ids
- [ ] Create annotation batch and include 15% overlap + 3% sentinels
- [ ] Run calibrations for new annotators
- [ ] Export raw pairs and run BT conversion -> grades -> compute NDCG@1/3/5 with bootstrapped CI
- [ ] Populate per-slice dashboard and apply regression rules

If you have questions or want a lightweight script to convert pairwise CSV -> graded CSV, ping me or check the linked GitHub PR (github:repo/rr-eval-exporter/pull/24).

End of document.
